sections.preamble: You are a coding assistant running inside pi, a coding agent harness. Help users inspect files, run commands, and modify code.
sections.tools:
<tools>
- read: Read file contents
- bash: Execute bash commands (ls, grep, find, etc.)
- edit: Make precise file edits with exact text replacement, including multiple disjoint edits in one call
- write: Create or overwrite files

Additional tools may be available.
</tools>
sections.rules:
<rules>
- Use bash for file operations like ls, rg, find
- Use read to examine files instead of cat or sed.
- You can inspect PI_* environment variables for current model and session details.
- Use edit for targeted changes. Batch changes to one file in a single call.
- Each edits[].oldText must exactly and uniquely match the original file. Keep matches short and non-overlapping; merge nearby changes without including large unchanged regions.
- Use write only for new files or complete rewrites.
- Be concise in your responses
- Show file paths clearly when working with files
</rules>

<project_instructions path="/home/julian/.pi/agent/AGENTS.md">
# Global instructions
As soon as your task is to programm something allways prioritize Test Driven Development (TDD) than do so.
Prefer simple, robust and performant solutions and check if something can get broken before making changes. Make sure to test against breaking changes.
<!-- pi-env:start (managed by setup-pi-tools.sh) -->
## Safety rules (all projects)
- Git: use only read-only git commands (status, diff, log, show, ls-files, rev-parse, blame). Never run `git init` or any other git command that changes or creates a repository, unless I ask for that exact command in my own message. A "yes" to another question is not such a request.
- Never delete directories recursively (`rm -r`, `rm -rf`) and never overwrite files outside the scope of the current task without asking me first.
- If a command is blocked by the confirmation-dialog extension or declined by me, do not retry it in another form (no `sh -c`, aliases, scripts, or full paths). Continue without it, or ask me to run it myself.
- Never create `.pi/` files or scan the whole directory when running directly in my home directory; ask which project directory is meant.

## Planning and memory
- When a task should be planned before it is executed (new feature, workflow change, larger bug), use the `plan` skill.
- If the project has `.pi/LOG.md`: after a compaction or at the start of a session, read `.pi/PLAN.md` and `tail -n 60 .pi/LOG.md` before doing anything else.

## CLI tools (call them via bash)
- `rg` (ripgrep): search code and text. Use `-n`, single-quoted patterns, `-M 200`; `-l` for file names only, `-F` for literal text, `-w` for whole words, `-U` for patterns spanning several lines. `rg --files -g '*name*'` finds files by name.
- `ctags -x --sort=no <file>`: outline of a file (functions, classes, methods with line numbers). Always use `-x`; without it ctags writes a `tags` file.
- `jq '<filter>' <file.json>`: query JSON (e.g. `jq '.scripts' package.json`) instead of reading the whole file.
- Read files with `read` and `offset`/`limit` instead of `cat`; check the length with `wc -l` first. Keep command output small (`| head -50`).
<!-- pi-env:end -->

</project_instructions>
</project_context>

path.description: Path to the file to read (relative or absolute)

offset.description: Line number to start reading from (1-indexed)

limit.description: Maximum number of lines to read

toolsAdded.name: bash
toolsAdded.description: Execute a bash command in the current working directory. Returns stdout and stderr. Output is truncated to last 2000 lines or 50KB (whichever is hit first). If truncated, full output is saved to a temp file. Optionally provide a timeout in seconds.

timeout.description: Timeout in seconds (optional, no default timeout)

toolsAdded.name: edit
toolsAdded.description: Edit a single file using exact text replacement. Every edits[].oldText must match a unique, non-overlapping region of the original file. If two changes affect the same block or nearby lines, merge them into one edit instead of emitting overlapping edits. Do not include large unchanged regions just to connect distant changes.

path.description: Path to the file to edit (relative or absolute)

oldText.description: Exact text for one targeted replacement. It must be unique in the original file and must not overlap with any other edits[].oldText in the same call.

newText.description: Replacement text for this targeted edit.

edits.description: One or more targeted replacements. Each edit is matched against the original file, not incrementally. Do not include overlapping or nested edits. If two changes touch the same block or nearby lines, merge them into one edit instead.

# PLAN.md — Active Technical Implementation Plan & State Anchor
> Created: 2026-11-04 15:32 · Baseline: `baseline/2026-11-04_1532/` (empty — every file in the map is new) · Git: 32e7bf2 (repo root `/home/julian/.pi/agent`) · Status: active · Last verified: 2026-11-04 16:45 (Step 4 e2e ALL PASSED; Step 5 scope guard + live /efforts show on real server OK)
> After a compaction or in a new session: read this file and `tail -n 60 LOG.md` before doing anything else.

## 1. Human Requirement (Original Intent)
Per-model reasoning (thinking) effort options in the pi TUI: each LM Studio model should expose its own array of efforts, togglable with shift+Tab; the API call to the LM Studio server must send the matching effort value; options must update when a session starts, when models are (re)loaded, or when a model is manually changed — with **no periodic polling**, prioritizing pi's native features. If the LM Studio API already reports a model's possible reasoning efforts, those should drive the options.

**Research result (done, 2026-11-04):**
- Pi already delivers the whole per-model mechanism natively: model `reasoning` flag + `thinkingLevelMap` (null = level hidden; `xhigh`/`max` only when explicitly mapped) → shift+Tab (`app.thinking.cycle`) re-derives the available levels from the *current* model on every keypress (`agent-session.js:2156` `cycleThinkingLevel` → `getSupportedThinkingLevels`, pi-ai `models.js:694`); model switches natively clamp the level; openai-completions sends the mapped value as `reasoning_effort` when `compat.supportsReasoningEffort`.
- The existing `extensions/lmstudio.ts` already wires this: dynamic model discovery, `efforts.json` auto-entries (`ensureModels`), per-model `thinkingLevelMap`, and refreshes at exactly the native moments the user named (startup registration, `/model` open, `/lmstudio`, `/reload`).
- **The LM Studio 0.4.28 API does NOT expose per-model supported reasoning efforts** (probed live on the running server: `/api/v0/models`, `/api/v0/models/{id}`, `/v1/models` — model object has only `id/object/type/publisher/arch/compatibility_type/quantization/state/max_context_length/loaded_context_length/capabilities`; `capabilities` carries e.g. `tool_use`, no effort data). → `efforts.json` remains the source of truth for the per-model effort array; the "use API data if present" branch is therefore not implemented (would be pure speculation about a field that doesn't exist).

## 2. Technical Architecture & Data Flow
- **Core Mechanism:** The only new runtime surface is a small `/efforts` TUI command in a new extension: it manages the per-model effort array in the existing `efforts.json` (set: listed levels keep their existing value or `DEFAULT_ENTRY` value, unlisted → null; show: current toggleable list). It then triggers the **existing native refresh** (`ctx.modelRegistry.refresh({providers:["lmstudio"], force:true, allowNetwork:true})` re-runs the existing `refreshModels` → new model objects with fresh `thinkingLevelMap`) and swaps the active model object via `pi.setModel(fresh)` — guarded so it fires only when the current model's option set actually changed (side effect: one `model_change` session entry; `setModel` also re-clamps the level). After that, 100% native: shift+Tab cycles the new set, model switches clamp, and the provider sends the mapped `reasoning_effort`.
- **Data / Control Flow:** `/efforts off,low,high,xhigh` -> (pure) `parseLevelsArg` -> (existing pure) write `efforts.json` -> native `refreshModels` (existing `extensions/lmstudio.ts`) -> registry snapshot rebuild -> guarded `pi.setModel(fresh)` -> native shift+Tab cycle + native `reasoning_effort` mapping. External `efforts.json` edits need no watcher: they apply at the next native refresh (session start / `/model` / `/lmstudio`), which is exactly the cadence the user specified.
- **Reuse & Conventions:** `projects/lmstudio/lmstudio-efforts.ts` (`PI_LEVELS`, `DEFAULT_ENTRY`, `loadEfforts`, `ensureModels`, `effortsFileUrl`); `extensions/lmstudio.ts` refresh + `/lmstudio` command pattern (untouched); sibling e2e harness `projects/lmstudio/e2e.mjs` (mock LM Studio server, `PI_*` env stripping, `/tmp` child cwd, captured `reasoning_effort` payloads); e2e control channel = pi RPC mode (`pi --mode rpc`, JSONL; commands `get_state`, `get_available_thinking_levels`, `set_model`, `prompt` — extension commands execute via `prompt`).
- **Acceptance Criteria:**
  1. `/efforts` (no args) on an LM Studio reasoning model shows its current toggleable level list (and the efforts file path); clear notification for non-LM-Studio or non-reasoning models.
  2. `/efforts off,low,high,xhigh` changes the active model's shift+Tab set to exactly that list **without restart** (proven via RPC `get_available_thinking_levels` before/after).
  3. After a set, the next chat request sends the mapped value as `reasoning_effort` (mock server capture); the file on disk holds the array (unlisted levels `null`).
  4. A model that appears on the LM Studio server is picked up at the next native refresh (`/lmstudio`) with an auto-created default entry; selecting it yields the full default option set (native path, e2e-proven).
  5. Invalid level tokens are rejected with the valid list shown; `efforts.json` is left unmodified.
  6. Scope guard: `git status` shows no changes to `extensions/lmstudio.ts` or anything under `projects/lmstudio/`.

## 3. Surgical File Map (Strict Scope Boundary)
- `projects/dynamic-readoning-levels/dynamic-efforts.ts` (NEW; pure, no pi imports, symbols `parseLevelsArg`, `applyEffortArray`, `optionsDiffer`, `levelsFromModel`: arg parsing for `/efforts <list>`, array→`ModelEntry` conversion reusing `PI_LEVELS`/`DEFAULT_ENTRY`/`ModelEntry` from `../lmstudio/lmstudio-efforts.ts`, option-set comparison for the guarded `setModel`, and a local mirror of pi-ai `getSupportedThinkingLevels` semantics for display — null hides, xhigh/max need explicit mapping)
- `projects/dynamic-readoning-levels/dynamic-efforts.test.mjs` (NEW; node:test unit suite for the pure module: valid/invalid/empty/case/whitespace parsing, value keep vs DEFAULT backfill, null-out of unlisted, optionsDiffer true/false cases, levelsFromModel semantics incl. non-reasoning model → `["off"]`)
- `extensions/dynamic-thinking-levels.ts` (NEW; wiring only: `pi.registerCommand("efforts", …)` — show + set; set path = `loadEfforts` → `applyEffortArray` → write file (2-space JSON + trailing newline, same format as `ensureModels`) → `ctx.modelRegistry.refresh({providers:["lmstudio"], force:true, allowNetwork:true, signal})` → if current model is `lmstudio` and `optionsDiffer(fresh, current)` then `pi.setModel(fresh)`; guards: non-lmstudio current model, refresh error (server down → `refreshModels` returns stale list, detect via `result.errors`/unchanged options and notify), invalid args never write)
- `projects/dynamic-readoning-levels/e2e.mjs` (NEW; mock LM Studio server + real `pi --mode rpc` child with session in `/tmp` cwd, env `LM_STUDIO_BASE_URL`/`LM_STUDIO_EFFORTS_FILE` pointing at temp file; scenarios AC2–AC4)

REMAINING (user, interactive TUI): `/efforts off,low,high` in the TUI, shift+Tab cycles exactly that set, next reply's request carries the mapped `reasoning_effort`

## 5. Negative Knowledge (Guardrails & Taboos)
- **Do NOT touch:** `extensions/lmstudio.ts`, anything under `projects/lmstudio/` (incl. `efforts.json` at rest — it is written only at runtime by pi), the pi runtime under `install/`, any other extension.
- **Do NOT add:** polling timers, `fs.watch`, lifecycle hooks (`session_start`/`session_shutdown`) — the extension holds no background resources (explicit user decision: native refresh moments are the update cadence).
- **Known Pitfalls / Failed Approaches:**
  - pi's built-in `DEFAULT_THINKING_LEVEL` is `"medium"` — e2e assertions on the off/low paths must set the level explicitly.
  - RPC/print child processes must strip all `PI_*` env vars (else they resume the live session) and run from a `/tmp` cwd (project trust prompt).
  - `ModelRuntime.registerProvider` (re-registration) resets the snapshot to the config's **static** `models` list — do NOT re-register to update models; use `refresh({force:true})` + guarded `pi.setModel`.
  - `pi.setModel` appends a `model_change` session entry unconditionally — hence the `optionsDiffer` guard before calling it.
  - `getSupportedThinkingLevels` semantics: null hides ANY level (incl. `off`); `xhigh`/`max` require an explicit non-null mapping; non-reasoning models only ever expose `["off"]`.
  - If LM Studio's API ever exposes per-model effort support, the natural hook is the existing `refreshModels` (merge server data into `thinkingLevelMap`); today the field does not exist, so nothing is implemented for it.
  - efforts.json semantics (existing extension, user confusion 2026-11-04): a **missing** level key is backfilled from `DEFAULT_ENTRY` by `ensureModels` at every refresh (model load!) → level stays VISIBLE; only an explicit **`null`** hides a level and survives backfill. So a hand-written 4-key entry silently becomes 7 visible levels. The TUI way to set an array is `/efforts <list>` (writes explicit nulls). Changing missing→null semantics would require editing the existing `projects/lmstudio` extension (out of scope here) and re-checking `openai-completions.js:621` (`map[level] ?? level` — null would send `reasoning_effort: null`).

## 6. Next Immediate Action
- **Target:** user's interactive TUI verification (no code changes expected).
- **Steps:** in a normal pi TUI session on the LM Studio model: (1) `/efforts off,low,high` → expect notify "shift+Tab levels now: off, low, high"; (2) shift+Tab cycles exactly off→low→high; (3) send a prompt → LM Studio request carries `reasoning_effort` = mapped value (off→none, low→low, high→high for the default entry); (4) `/efforts` (no args) shows the set; (5) optionally: load a different model in LM Studio, run `/lmstudio`, select it → full default set.
